_note: The numinosum: the term from Rudolf Otto (CW11 ¶6, ¶9), the effect it has (CW8 ¶216, CW18 ¶787), that it is never indifferent (CW8 ¶405), how it is met in a life (CW10 ¶871, ¶874, ¶864) and its place beside dogma (CW18 ¶1160). Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: Jung's uses of Otto's word: its definition in CW11 ¶6, and later passages in CW8, CW10 and CW18.

sections.title: The term
sections.line: CW11 ¶6 and ¶9 (Psychology and Religion): Jung credits Rudolf Otto with the word and gives his own definition; ¶9 on religion and the experience of the numinosum.

quotes.quote: On the contrary, it seizes and controls the human subject, who is always rather its victim than its creator.
The numinosum is either a quality belonging to a visible object or the influence of an invisible presence that causes a peculiar alteration of consciousness.
the attitude peculiar to a consciousness which has been changed by experience of the numinosum

sections.title: What it does to a person
sections.line: CW8 ¶216, where Jung again credits Otto's expression, and CW18 ¶787, where he lists what belongs to a nocturnal, numinous experience.

quotes.quote: the numinosum, to use an apt expression of Rudolf Otto's

An integral component of any nocturnal, numinous experience is the dimming of consciousness, the feeling that one is in the grip of something greater than oneself, the impossibility of exercising criticism, and the paralysis of the will

sections.title: Never indifferent
sections.line: CW8 ¶405: Jung on the numinous character of the archetypes when they appear, and on its effects.

quotes.quote: the archetypes have, when they appear, a distinctly numinous character which can only be described as "spiritual," if "magical" is too strong a word
It can be healing or destructive, but never indifferent, provided of course that it has attained a certain degree of clarity.

sections.title: In a life
sections.line: CW10 ¶864, ¶871 and ¶874 (Good and Evil in Analytical Psychology): the numinosum, the tremendum and the fascinosum.

quotes.quote: Anything that comes upon me with this intensity I experience as numinous, no matter whether I call it divine or devilish or just “fate.”
Consciousness experiences this supraordinate totality as something numinous, as a tremendum or fascinosum
I am face to face with what Rudolf Otto calls the tremendum and fascinosum. I cannot "conquer" a numinosum, I can only open myself to it, let myself be overpowered by it, trusting in its meaning

sections.title: And the doctrines
sections.line: CW18 ¶1160: the numinous quality of the archetypes, and what Jung says follows for theology.

quotes.quote: As the archetypes have a “numinous” quality and underlie all religious and dogmatic ideas, depth psychology is also of importance for theology.
